title: X2KNWLDG extraction bundle
description: The bundle an extraction produces before it becomes canonical output, for **both** implemented media. One bundle describes one run and a run declares one medium (`artifacts.MEDIUM_PROFILES`), so the top-level `oneOf` is that dispatch: YouTube coverage is a timeline of `windows` and a claim cites seconds; Twitter coverage is a set of `items` and a claim cites a post id and a character span. This document was YouTube-only long after `apply-bundle` began accepting Twitter bundles, so every committed Twitter fixture — each of which the shipped gate passes — was refused here, and `mcp_server.extraction_schema_resource` served the refusal to agents as the contract. Knowledge unit ids must be usable as one segment of a three-part global id (D-011): no colon, no whitespace, no leading dot, so that '.' and '..' can never appear. src/x2knwldg/ids.py is the single implementation of that rule and validators.py enforces it at validation time (D-018).

coverage.$comment: One coverage document with **both** shapes declared, and the top-level `allOf` branch saying which of them a given bundle must carry. `windows` is the YouTube timeline `validators.validate_coverage` walks; `items` is the Twitter set `validators.validate_item_coverage` compares. `required` here names only what both media carry, so the branch — not this clause — is what refuses a Twitter document for having no windows.

audit_attempts.$comment: minimum 0, not 1: coverage.create_pending_coverage writes 0 into every fresh run, WORKFLOW.md §4.4 and prompts/05 both describe 0 as the honest never-audited state, and validators.validate_coverage accepts 0 while refusing it alongside a PASS claim (unaudited_coverage_pass). The schema was the one artifact of the four that rejected the document the pipeline actually produces. maximum is constants.MAX_AUDIT_ATTEMPTS, asserted against it in tests/test_index_schemas.py.

window_size_sec.$comment: Declared here for the first time, and it is required in the only sense the validator uses the word: `validators.validate_coverage` emits `missing_window_size` when a document claims `PASS` without it, and measures every window against it. So a bundle could validate here with zero errors and come back from `x2knwldg validate` as coverage `FAIL` — the same asymmetry D-092 and D-169 are about, one field along. Only the `apply-bundle` path hid it, because `artifacts._carry_coverage_scaffold_forward` restores the scaffold's value before any validator runs. `maximum` is `constants.COVERAGE_WINDOW_SEC`, the widest window the format has: an audit may subdivide a scaffolded window and may not widen one (D-164).

status.$comment: The window vocabulary is constants.COVERAGE_STATUSES. `pending` was missing while coverage.py wrote it into every window of a fresh run, so the schema described a document the code does not produce.

items.$comment: D-092: this was a bare object schema with no properties, so it accepted an entry keyed `reason` that validators.validate_coverage then rejected as `invalid_omission_reason` naming null - and the key names appeared only in validators.py and an archival spec the workflow never links. The vocabulary is constants.OMISSION_REASONS, asserted against it in tests/test_index_schemas.py.

type.$comment: The controlled vocabulary is constants.OMISSION_REASONS and tests/test_index_schemas.py asserts this enum equals it. `source_unavailable` joined for T-227 (D-225): an included post that was never observed has no content to audit, and the omission is minted by the pipeline rather than chosen by an auditor, so it is a named reason and not `other_explained`.

note.$comment: `\\S` rather than minLength alone: validate_coverage tests str(note).strip(), so a note of only spaces is a missing explanation to it and would be an accepted one here. The two gates must not disagree.

basis.$comment: `validators.validate_item_coverage` refuses a document whose basis is not `items` (`coverage_basis_not_items`), because a time-window document read as an item document would report every post missing. Not constrained to a `const` here: the gate imposes the capture's value before validating, so a schema that refused a bundle stating something else would refuse a bundle `apply-bundle` accepts.

items.$comment: Only `post_id` and `status` are required, and that is the validator's own rule rather than a relaxation of the window shape: `validate_item_coverage` refuses an entry with no post id or an unknown status, and checks the three lists only when they are present. `item_id` is minted by the scaffold and carried.

status.$comment: The window vocabulary is constants.COVERAGE_STATUSES. `pending` was missing while coverage.py wrote it into every window of a fresh run, so the schema described a document the code does not produce.

items.$comment: D-092: this was a bare object schema with no properties, so it accepted an entry keyed `reason` that validators.validate_coverage then rejected as `invalid_omission_reason` naming null - and the key names appeared only in validators.py and an archival spec the workflow never links. The vocabulary is constants.OMISSION_REASONS, asserted against it in tests/test_index_schemas.py.

type.$comment: The controlled vocabulary is constants.OMISSION_REASONS and tests/test_index_schemas.py asserts this enum equals it. `source_unavailable` joined for T-227 (D-225): an included post that was never observed has no content to audit, and the omission is minted by the pipeline rather than chosen by an auditor, so it is a named reason and not `other_explained`.

note.$comment: `\\S` rather than minLength alone: validate_coverage tests str(note).strip(), so a note of only spaces is a missing explanation to it and would be an accepted one here. The two gates must not disagree.

allOf.$comment: The medium branch, and the reason it is a discriminator rather than a declared field: a bundle carries no `source_type` — the run does, in `metadata.json`, and that is what `artifacts._profile_for` dispatches on (D-240, D-243). What the bundle carries is the difference itself, so the branch reads it. `else` rather than a second `if` on `windows`, so a coverage document with neither is reported as a YouTube document missing `windows` instead of as matching no branch at all.

then.$comment: A Twitter/X run: item coverage, and a claim that cites a post id and a character span.

else.$comment: A YouTube run: a timeline of windows, and a claim that cites seconds.

kind.$comment: constants.KNOWLEDGE_KINDS, drift-tested in tests/test_index_schemas.py. `canonical_concept` is deliberately absent: library.py mints it for a concept node and no bundle carries one. This used to be `type: string, minLength: 1`, so a model that validated its output against the published schema still got `invalid_kind` out of validators.py — the schema blessed a bundle apply-bundle then rejected.

allOf.$comment: `validators.validate_knowledge_units`: `requires_provenance = source_class == "source" or kind in SOURCE_KINDS`, so the obligation follows the kind as well as the declaration and a unit cannot shed it by mislabelling itself. The obligation is medium-neutral — a provenance-bearing unit carries a `source` object in both media — so it is stated once here. *Which* fields that object must carry is the one thing that differs, and it is the top-level `oneOf`'s business (`validators.PROVENANCE_FIELDS`). The schema required no `source` block at all, so a `source_class: "source"` unit without one validated here and came back `missing_source`.

youtubeUnit.$comment: The YouTube provenance field set, applied under the same condition — referenced rather than restated, so the rule about *when* provenance is owed has one home.

twitterUnit.$comment: The Twitter provenance field set, applied under the same condition — referenced rather than restated, so the rule about *when* provenance is owed has one home.

twitterSource.$comment: `validators.PROVENANCE_FIELDS["twitter"]`. A post id and an exact character span, and **no seconds**: `WORKFLOW.md` §T3 puts it as "a claim that carries `start_sec` is a claim in the wrong shape". The excerpt is `text.canonical[start_char:end_char]` compared byte for byte — `validate_post_provenance`'s `evidence_excerpt_is_not_its_span` — because normalizing either side would discard the ZWNJ, NBSP and Persian digits a Persian post is made of (D-211). Offsets are codepoints and an empty span cites nothing, so `end_char` must exceed `start_char`; that comparison is `validate_post_provenance`'s, since JSON Schema compares no two fields.

relation.$comment: constants.RELATION_TYPES, drift-tested in tests/test_index_schemas.py. It used to be a bare `type: string` with no enum and no minLength, so `""` and `folklore` both validated and both came back `invalid_relation`.
